--- title: "Statistical tests" subtitle: "Day 3 - Introduction to Data Analysis with R" author: "Selina Baldauf" institute: "Freie Universität Berlin - Theoretical Ecology" date: today date-format: long format: revealjs: footer: "Selina Baldauf // Statistical tests" highlight-style: breeze mainfont: Cabinet Grotesk slide-number: true show-slide-number: all incremental: true self-contained: true code-line-numbers: false auto-stretch: false scrollable: false theme: slides.scss fig-align: center fig-width: 6.3 fig-height: 6.3 execute: echo: true warning: false message: false cache: true knitr: opts_chunk: collapse: true comment: "#>" from: markdown+emoji filters: - roughnotation - flourish --- ## General approach ![](img/day3/statistics_approach.png){width="70%"} :::{.aside} Please note the discussion about p-values as a basis for binary decisions. See e.g. [here](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-019-0470-3) or [here](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-00857-9) as a starting point ::: ## Tests to compare two groups :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} :::{.fragment} **t-test** ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: :::{.fragment} :::{.nonincremental} - Compares the **means** of two groups - Suitable for roughly normal data, or for larger samples - 2 versions: Student's (equal variance) and Welch's t-test - Welch's t-test is a good default ::: ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} :::{.fragment} **Wilcoxon rank-sum test** ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: :::{.nonincremental} - Compares **ranks**: does one group tend to have larger values? - Useful for ordinal data, skewed small samples, or outliers ::: ::: ::: ::: . . . ## The data: iris **Question:** Does the sepal width differ between *I. versicolor* and *I. virginica*? :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Reproduce the data"} flowers <- as_tibble(iris) |> filter(Species %in% c("versicolor", "virginica")) |> select(sepal_width = Sepal.Width, species = Species) |> droplevels() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flowers #> # A tibble: 100 × 2 #> sepal_width species #> #> 1 3.2 versicolor #> 2 3.2 versicolor #> 3 3.1 versicolor #> 4 2.3 versicolor #> 5 2.8 versicolor #> 6 2.8 versicolor #> 7 3.3 versicolor #> 8 2.4 versicolor #> 9 2.9 versicolor #> 10 2.7 versicolor #> # ℹ 90 more rows ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ![Image from [medium.com](https://medium.com/data-science/k-medoids-clustering-on-iris-data-set-1931bf781e05)](img/day3/iris.png) Sepal width (in cm) of 50 flowers from each of two iris species ::: ::: ## First look at the data :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flowers |> summarize( n = n(), mean = mean(sepal_width), sd = sd(sepal_width), .by = species ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #> species n mean sd #> #> 1 versicolor 50 2.77 0.314 #> 2 virginica 50 2.97 0.322 ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Code for the boxplot"} ggplot(flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)) + geom_boxplot() + geom_point( position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 123), alpha = 0.6 ) + labs(x = "Species", y = "Sepal width (cm)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Prepare the group vectors Most test functions take the values of each group as a vector ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} versicolor <- filter(flowers, species == "versicolor")$sepal_width virginica <- filter(flowers, species == "virginica")$sepal_width ``` ::: . . .
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} versicolor #> [1] 3.2 3.2 3.1 2.3 2.8 2.8 3.3 2.4 2.9 2.7 2.0 3.0 2.2 2.9 2.9 3.1 3.0 2.7 2.2 #> [20] 2.5 3.2 2.8 2.5 2.8 2.9 3.0 2.8 3.0 2.9 2.6 2.4 2.4 2.7 2.7 3.0 3.4 3.1 2.3 #> [39] 3.0 2.5 2.6 3.0 2.6 2.3 2.7 3.0 2.9 2.9 2.5 2.8 ``` ::: ## Shapiro-Wilk test for normality . . . $H_0$: The data come from a normal distribution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shapiro.test(versicolor) #> #> Shapiro-Wilk normality test #> #> data: versicolor #> W = 0.97413, p-value = 0.338 shapiro.test(virginica) #> #> Shapiro-Wilk normality test #> #> data: virginica #> W = 0.96739, p-value = 0.1809 ``` ::: - A **large p-value**: no evidence against normality, can not reject $H_0$ - With large samples, very small deviations can give small p-values - Always look at the data as well ## Normality with QQ-plots Points should roughly follow the line. Look at the **tails** and at **unusual observations**. :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggpubr::ggqqplot(versicolor) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggpubr::ggqqplot(virginica) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: ::: . . . Both species: no clear deviation from normality ## What does non-normal data look like? :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Compare two means: Welch's t-test $H_0$: The means of the two groups do not differ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} t.test(versicolor, virginica) #> #> Welch Two Sample t-test #> #> data: versicolor and virginica #> t = -3.2058, df = 97.927, p-value = 0.001819 #> alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0 #> 95 percent confidence interval: #> -0.33028364 -0.07771636 #> sample estimates: #> mean of x mean of y #> 2.770 2.974 ``` ::: - t: test statistic (t = 0 if the means are equal) - p-value: How likely is a difference at least this large if the means were equal? - Reject $H_0$ . . . Mean sepal width was **0.20 cm smaller** in *I. versicolor* than in *I. virginica* (Welch's t-test, $t_{97.9}$ = -3.21, p = 0.002). ## Wilcoxon rank-sum test $H_0$: Neither group tends to have larger values than the other - All values are ranked from smallest to largest - The test compares the ranks of the two groups - **Demonstration only:** the iris data don't need a rank-based test, t-test was fine here . . . ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} wilcox.test(versicolor, virginica) #> #> Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction #> #> data: versicolor and virginica #> W = 841, p-value = 0.004572 #> alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0 ``` ::: . . . Sepal width tended to be smaller in *I. versicolor* than in *I. virginica* (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, W = 841, p = 0.005). ## Paired observations Examples of paired observations: :::{.nonincremental} - Blood pressure of patients before and after medication - Difference in sleep quality of people as children and adults - Biodiversity in rivers before and after a power plant ... ::: . . . In `sleep`, the **same 10 people** received two drugs (`extra`: extra sleep in hours) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Reproduce the data"} sleep_paired <- sleep |> pivot_wider( names_from = group, names_prefix = "drug_", values_from = extra ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sleep_paired #> # A tibble: 10 × 3 #> ID drug_1 drug_2 #> #> 1 1 0.7 1.9 #> 2 2 -1.6 0.8 #> 3 3 -0.2 1.1 #> 4 4 -1.2 0.1 #> 5 5 -0.1 -0.1 #> 6 6 3.4 4.4 #> 7 7 3.7 5.5 #> 8 8 0.8 1.6 #> 9 9 0 4.6 #> 10 10 2 3.4 ``` ::: ## Paired observations ::: {.cell flourish='[{"target":"paired = TRUE"}]'} ```{.r .cell-code} t.test( sleep_paired$drug_1, sleep_paired$drug_2, paired = TRUE ) #> #> Paired t-test #> #> data: sleep_paired$drug_1 and sleep_paired$drug_2 #> t = -4.0621, df = 9, p-value = 0.002833 #> alternative hypothesis: true mean difference is not equal to 0 #> 95 percent confidence interval: #> -2.4598858 -0.7001142 #> sample estimates: #> mean difference #> -1.58 ``` ::: Also: `wilcox.test(..., paired = TRUE)` . . . People slept **1.58 h longer** with drug 2 than with drug 1 (paired t-test, $t_9$ = -4.06, p = 0.003). # Visualizing test results {.inverse} ## Boxplot to show differences ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + geom_boxplot() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: ## Add a test with `geom_signif()` The [`ggsignif`](https://const-ae.github.io/ggsignif/) package adds significance levels to a ggplot ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("ggsignif") library(ggsignif) ggplot( flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + geom_boxplot() + geom_signif( comparisons = list( c("versicolor", "virginica") ), test = "t.test", map_signif_level = TRUE ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: :::{.nonincremental} - `test = "t.test"`: Welch's t-test (the default is a Wilcoxon test) - `map_signif_level = TRUE`: stars, `FALSE`: p-value ::: ## Plot means with `stat_summary()` ::: {.cell output-location='column' flourish='[{"target":"stat_summary()"}]'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + stat_summary() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: :::{.nonincremental} - By default, `stat_summary()` shows the mean ± standard error (SE) ::: ## Style means and error bars ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + stat_summary( fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.15 ) + stat_summary( fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "#28a87d", size = 4 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: :::{.nonincremental} - `fun.data` for error bars, `fun` for points ::: ## Barplots with error bars ::: {.cell output-location='column' flourish='[{"target-rx":"geom = .bar."}]'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + stat_summary( fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.15 ) + stat_summary( fun = mean, geom = "bar", fill = "#28a87d", width = 0.65 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: ## Add the test to the barplot :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + stat_summary( fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.15 ) + stat_summary( fun = mean, geom = "bar", fill = "#28a87d", width = 0.65 ) + geom_signif( comparisons = list( c("versicolor", "virginica") ), test = "t.test", map_signif_level = TRUE ) ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-29-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: ::: ::: # Comparing three groups {.inverse} ## Actually, there were three species **Question:** Does the sepal width differ between the three iris species? :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Reproduce the data"} flowers_all <- as_tibble(iris) |> select(sepal_width = Sepal.Width, species = Species) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flowers_all |> summarize( n = n(), mean = mean(sepal_width), .by = species ) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #> species n mean #> #> 1 setosa 50 3.43 #> 2 versicolor 50 2.77 #> 3 virginica 50 2.97 ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-32-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: ::: ::: . . . Could we just run 3 separate t-tests? ## Two kinds of errors Every test decision can be wrong in two ways: | | $H_0$ is true (no difference) | $H_0$ is false (real difference) | |---|---|---| | **Reject $H_0$** | **Type I error**: false positive (probability α) | Correct | | **Do not reject $H_0$** | Correct | **Type II error**: false negative | . . . - With α = 0.05, we accept a 5% risk of a false positive - Multiple testing increases the risk of a **type I error** ## Error-inflation with multiple testing - For one test: Chance of false positive is 5% (at α = 0.05) - This error potential increases with multiple tests: . . . $$P(\text{at least one false positive}) = 1 - (1 - \alpha)^k$$ with $k$ = number of tests . . . | Number of tests | Chance of at least one false positive | |---:|---:| | 1 | 5% | | 3 | 14.3% | | 10 | 40.1% | . . . Solution: p-value correction for multiple testing ## Pairwise comparisons in R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairwise.t.test( flowers_all$sepal_width, flowers_all$species, pool.sd = FALSE ) #> #> Pairwise comparisons using t tests with non-pooled SD #> #> data: flowers_all$sepal_width and flowers_all$species #> #> setosa versicolor #> versicolor 7.5e-15 - #> virginica 9.1e-09 0.0018 #> #> P value adjustment method: holm ``` ::: :::{.nonincremental} - `pool.sd = FALSE`: Welch's t-test for each pair (the default uses one shared SD across all groups) - The p-values are already adjusted (Holm method is the default) - Rank-based alternative: `pairwise.wilcox.test()` ::: ## Add the adjusted p-values to a plot `geom_signif` can't run pairwise tests, so we need to add p-values manually. ::: {.cell output-location='column' flourish='[{"target":"annotations = c"},{"target":"step_increase = 0.1,"}]'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers_all, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + geom_boxplot() + geom_signif( comparisons = list( c("setosa", "versicolor"), c("setosa", "virginica"), c("versicolor", "virginica") ), annotations = c( "p = 7.5e-15", "p = 9.1e-09", "p = 0.0018" ), step_increase = 0.1, tip_length = 0.02 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-34-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: :::{.nonincremental} - `annotations`: show our adjusted p-values (no new tests) - `step_increase`: stack the brackets ::: ## Extract the p-values automatically Typing p-values by hand is error-prone. Extract them with `p["row", "column"]`: :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairwise_results <- pairwise.t.test( flowers_all$sepal_width, flowers_all$species, pool.sd = FALSE ) p <- pairwise_results$p.value comparisons <- list( c("setosa", "versicolor"), c("setosa", "virginica"), c("versicolor", "virginica") ) adjusted_p <- c( p["versicolor", "setosa"], p["virginica", "setosa"], p["virginica", "versicolor"] ) p_labels <- paste( "p =", format.pval(adjusted_p, digits = 2) ) ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers_all, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + geom_boxplot() + geom_signif( comparisons = comparisons, annotations = p_labels, step_increase = 0.1, tip_length = 0.02 ) ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Add the test results to the barplot :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( flowers_all, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width) ) + stat_summary( fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.15 ) + stat_summary( fun = mean, geom = "bar", fill = "#28a87d", width = 0.65 ) + geom_signif( comparisons = comparisons, annotations = p_labels, step_increase = 0.1, tip_length = 0.02 ) ``` ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](tests_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-38-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: ::: ::: # Now you {.inverse} [Task (45 min)]{.highlight-blue}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
